name: Eric Romero
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember replacing old menus by hand on the night of a rent rise.” People around Studio Boulevard know Eric by a small Monday habit. Eric waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I own the restaurant and cannot feed a table at last year's rent. I can still bring out their old candleholder.
appearance: Eric is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it, Eric takes off the watch before a long conversation when listening.
personality: Eric loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To give the family their candleholder despite the small order.
family: Remy Rose is Eric’s stepsibling. Eric calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Remy leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *One paid trial*, Remy says, “I can take morning deliveries for one week so both bakers get a fair turn at the oven.”
connections: Esme Knight (landlord). The restaurant and its landlord have to work out what another expensive summer actually earns.

reactions.situation: A relative tries to pay the whole restaurant bill in secret
reactions.response: Eric speaks to the host privately and lets them decide whether the bill is shared.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Eric asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.

reactions.response: Eric offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
